Selection Sort Analysis

Complexity Profile

  • Best Case Time: O(N²)
  • Average Case Time: O(N²)
  • Worst Case Time: O(N²)
  • Space Complexity: O(1) (Auxiliary)

How it Works

Selection Sort divides the array into a sorted and an unsorted part. It repeatedly searches the unsorted part to find the minimum element, and then swaps it with the first element of the unsorted part, growing the sorted part by one element on each iteration.

Advantages

  • Very simple to understand and implement.
  • Performs minimal swaps: O(N) swaps in the worst case, making it useful when write operations are expensive (e.g. flash memory).
  • Operates **in-place** (uses no extra memory).

Disadvantages

  • Extremely inefficient for large datasets.
  • Time complexity is always O(N²), even if the array is already sorted.
  • It is unstable (can change the relative order of elements with equal values).

Quick Sort Analysis

Complexity Profile

  • Best Case Time: O(N log N)
  • Average Case Time: O(N log N)
  • Worst Case Time: O(N²)
  • Space Complexity: O(log N) (Call Stack)

How it Works

Quick Sort is a Divide-and-Conquer algorithm. It selects a "pivot" element from the array and partitions the other elements into two sub-arrays, according to whether they are less than or greater than the pivot. It then recursively sorts the sub-arrays.

Advantages

  • Extremely fast in practice (often faster than Merge Sort or Heap Sort on real-world datasets).
  • Operates in-place, requiring only O(log N) extra space for recursive stack frames.
  • Has excellent cache locality.

Disadvantages

  • Worst-case performance is O(N²) (occurs when the pivot selection consistently chooses the smallest or largest element).
  • Not stable (can change relative order of identical elements).
  • Recursive implementation can cause StackOverflow on extremely large, poorly partitioned datasets if not optimized.

💻 Java Implementations Side-by-Side

These are the exact algorithms running in our Java console program:

Selection Sort (Java)

static void SelectionSort(int[] A) {
    int n = A.length;
    for (int i = 0; i < n - 1; i++) {
        int min_idx = i;
        for (int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) {
            if (A[j] < A[min_idx]) {
                min_idx = j;
            }
        }
        if (min_idx != i) {
            int temp = A[min_idx];
            A[min_idx] = A[i];
            A[i] = temp;
        }
    }
}

Quick Sort (Java)

static void QuickSort(int[] A, int LI, int RI) {
    int j;
    if (LI < RI) {
        j = Divide(A, LI, RI);
        QuickSort(A, LI, j - 1);
        QuickSort(A, j + 1, RI);
    }
}

static int Divide(int[] A, int LI, int RI) {
    int Pivot, j, i, Temp;
    Pivot = A[LI];
    i = LI;
    j = RI + 1;
    while (i < j) {
        do {
            i++;
        } while (i < RI && A[i] < Pivot);
        
        do {
            j--;
        } while (j > LI && A[j] > Pivot);
        
        if (i < j) {
            Temp = A[i];
            A[i] = A[j];
            A[j] = Temp;
        }
    }
    Temp = A[LI];
    A[LI] = A[j];
    A[j] = Temp;
    return j;
}
